The tested local value comes from FIREBASE_WEBAPP_CONFIG (f1:22, f1:25, s3).

The early returns enable or suppress the configuration fetch; only the continuation reaches that operation (f1:62, f1:67, f1:73, f1:78, s11).
The checks activate config retrieval for eligible configuration and platform values, with no analysis-detection predicate in this path (f1:62, f1:67, f1:73, f1:78, s11).
The code requires configuration and request credentials and reuses supplied configuration on the platform and demo branches, supporting data_availability (f1:62, f1:68, f1:74, f1:78, f1:89).
The fetch sink lies directly in s10 after all four early-return guards, requiring no witness hops (s4, s2, s7, s9, s11).
The sole fetch is inside getFinalConfig after all cited guards; its only caller is the promise continuation and there is no export or alternate entry to the sink (f1:61, f1:88, f1:124).
The fetch retrieves configuration JSON, which is returned and incorporated into generated defaults files, supporting benign build configuration work (f1:88, f1:103, f1:104, f1:127, f1:138).
The single early-return guard requires the trimmed environment value to be truthy before entering s12, so the combination has one condition (s5, s12).

The predicate activates configuration loading when a value is supplied; it does not detect an analysis environment (f1:25, s5, s12).
The guard skips loading when no usable configuration value is supplied, supporting data_availability (f1:25, s5, s12).
The readFile call is inside s12 on the continuation after s5, so the sink is directly in the guarded region (s5, s12, s13).
The sole readFile call is inside getPartialConfig after the cited guard, and getPartialConfig is invoked only by the top-level promise chain (f1:24, s5, f1:50, f1:122).
readFile is imported from node:fs/promises and loads JSON configuration subsequently used for generated defaults files (f1:18, f1:50, f1:51, f1:124, f1:138).
